title: The biggest video game of all time looks like a movie
summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI "extended look" resembles a prestige crime drama rather than a traditional video game trailer, reflecting the gaming industry's trend of blurring lines between Hollywood and gaming. The approach demonstrates Rockstar's strategy to maintain cultural dominance through cinematic production values.
content:
I think I know why Rockstar Games debuted its "extended look" of Grand Theft Auto VI on Netflix instead of immediately dropping it for free on YouTube. Unlike most video game trailers, the almost 27-minute preview of GTA VI felt more like a slice of a prestige crime drama than any video game trailer that I've ever seen. To make a new game that lasts another decade or more and potentially rivals the success of its predecessor, Rockstar is clearly trying to further blur the lines between Hollywood and video games.

title: GTA VI: all the news on Rockstar’s next entry in the Grand Theft Auto series
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI's release has been delayed to November 19, 2026. A new 'extended look' debuted on Netflix showing protagonists Jason and Lucia in Vice City with significantly improved graphics and detailed environments.
content:
It’s been over a decade and two console generations since GTA V came out, and its sequel is still a work in progress. GTA VI has faced multiple delays, with developer Rockstar Games bumping back its predicted release date twice, eventually shifting to November 19th, 2026, a full year after its originally planned fall 2025 release window. Early official glimpses offered a look at the game’s protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who players will navigate around Vice City as outlaws on the run after a job goes south.
Preorders have opened for the digital code-only game, offering the $79.99 standard edition and $99.99 Ultimate Edition on both PS5 and Xbox Series X / S.
Rockstar Games has also responded to “CyberLeek” posts that showed sequences of the game, calling them heartbreaking and saying, “…this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time.” At about the same time, the leakers released yet another clip.
Now a half-hour “extended look” has arrived full of gameplay slices and cutscenes that’s available for viewing on Netflix, as well as all over other social media channels in reaction videos before it hits YouTube at 9PM — here are some of our first impressions.
Read on below for all of the news and updates about Grand Theft Auto VI.

title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia achieved AGI, again — not that it matters
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang casually claimed the company achieved artificial general intelligence (AGI) during an earnings call before dismissing the milestone as "senseless" due to lack of consensus on what AGI actually means. The statement highlights ongoing debate about whether AGI is a meaningful technological goal or arbitrary marketing.
content:
On Nvidia's earnings call Wednesday, CEO Jensen Huang casually announced the company had "achieved AGI," one of the tech industry's ultimate goals some of its biggest players have spent years chasing. Almost immediately, Huang dismissed the coveted milestone as "senseless."   
He's right. For the supposed finish line of the AI race, there is no consensus on what artificial general intelligence means, let alone how we'll know when we've actually got there, which makes achieving it equally arbitrary. 
Asked about OpenAI's pursuit of AGI, Huang said that when it comes to Nvidia, "for many tasks, we could say that we've already achieved AGI."  …
Read the full story at The Verge.
